prompt: Which statement is true for **every** rectangle but **not** for every rhombus?

choices.label: The diagonals are congruent (equal in length)

hint: Both shapes are parallelograms, so anything true of all parallelograms will be true of both — those cannot be the answer.

hints.text: Both shapes are parallelograms, so anything true of all parallelograms will be true of both — those cannot be the answer.
Picture a long skinny rhombus (a squashed diamond). Are its two diagonals the same length?
No — one is long and one is short. But a rectangle's diagonals are always equal. Choice B.

explanation: A and C are true of every parallelogram, so they do not separate the two shapes.
D is true of every rhombus but false for a non-square rectangle — that is backwards from what the question asks.
B is the winner: rectangles always have congruent diagonals, while a squashed rhombus has one long and one short diagonal.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with extreme shapes
steps: Imagine a rhombus flattened almost to a line: the diagonals are wildly different lengths.
Now imagine any rectangle: both diagonals stretch corner to corner across the same rectangle, so they must match.
